top_story.headline: Drug Enforcement Administration sole-sources a spot in Detroit's Thanksgiving parade to promote its Fentanyl Free America Initiative
top_story.dek: The agency says only one organization, the parade's own foundation, can let its agents march in the parade.
paragraphs: The Drug Enforcement Administration plans to buy participation in the 2026 America's Thanksgiving Parade in Detroit from Michigan's Thanksgiving Parade Foundation without competition. The justification says participation will support the Fentanyl Free America Initiative by raising public awareness of illicit fentanyl. DEA members will walk in the parade carrying the American flag and a banner for the agency and the initiative. The Detroit Field Division is the requiring office, and performance starts November 26, 2026.

The agency's reason for skipping competition is that the foundation, founded in 1982, exists to stage and perpetuate the parade, so it is the only organization able to provide participation. The authority cited is the "only one responsible source" rule (FAR 6.103-1). The estimated amount is blank in the posted copy, so no value is available. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under the foundation's name. The notice was posted as a Special Notice, and the justification file is what identified it as a sole-source action.

sections.headline: General Services Administration seeks a five-year lease extension at 131 M Street NE in Washington without competition

The other four were listed in earlier editions and are left out: a Marine Barracks Washington curtain-cleaning solicitation, a State Department contractor job posting, a Transportation Security Administration PreCheck industry request and a fine-arts conservation sources sought notice. The justification says the current lease expires 9/7/2026, a date before the file was posted on November 2. No value is stated and the landlord is not named in the data.

paragraphs: There were 38 new sole-source justifications, 19 of them posted under other notice types, and 5 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The Drug Enforcement Administration parade purchase is today's Top Story, and ten extensions and bridges are in the Extensions section below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Army plans to keep MANTech running the Defense Commissary Agency's legacy computer systems with no competition
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command
blocks.text: The Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground intends to award MANTech Advanced Systems International, Inc. a one-year contract with four option years to run IT operations, custom software and databases for the Defense Commissary Agency across about 250 commissaries. The notice says the systems contain over 4,000 custom-coded processes in COBOL and other older languages, and that market research on 23 vendor capability statements found only the incumbent could avoid "catastrophic failure" as the systems are phased out over 24 to 36 months. A formal justification is still being coordinated. The file's properties list "Author: Gemini Enterprise" and a last-modified-by entry for an Army Contracting Command civilian employee. That is metadata only and does not show how much of the text an AI tool wrote. It was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs renews NetApp storage support through ThunderCat for $4.5 million, saying replacement would cost $52 million
meta: Skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Information and Technology awarded ThunderCat Technology, LLC a brand-name order for NetApp hardware and software maintenance, training and account-manager services on October 30, under NASA's SEWP V contract. The justification says replacing the storage with a new system would take about 12 months and cost roughly $52,000,000, "considering the current shortages in storage devices due to Artificial Intelligence demand." The storage holds data for veterans' benefits claims and medical records. It was posted as an Award Notice.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs plans to sole-source a University of Colorado research data system for a Montana medical center under a subject line about Thermo Fisher
meta: Regents of the University of Colorado Campus
blocks.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office 19 says it intends to award the Regents of the University of Colorado Campus a one-year deal with four options (December 4, 2026 to December 3, 2031) for the REDCap research data system and OnCore trial management system at the Fort Harrison VA Medical Center. The subject line reads "Preventive Maintenance Services for Thermo Fisher", which does not match the body. The office says the services are proprietary to the university. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this name. Responses are due 9:00 a.m. Mountain time on November 9. It was posted as a Special Notice.

sections.headline: Labor Department extends Education and Training Resources' Wilmington Job Corps Center operation for up to $10.6 million without competition, citing two federal court orders
paragraphs: There were ten new extensions and bridges today, covering a Job Corps center, a city sewer system, a federal prison medical contract and several leases.

blocks.title: Labor Department keeps Education and Training Resources running the Wilmington Job Corps Center without competition while court orders and a recompete play out
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of Labor asks to award Education and Training Resources, the current operator, a one-year contract of $7,548,685 from November 1, 2026, plus a six-month extension of $3,057,697 through April 30, 2028. The incumbent contract expired October 31, 2026. The justification says the "administration of Job Corps program is subject to two federal court orders" while the department assesses plans for a competitive procurement. The center is a 24-hour residential operation, and the department estimates it would cost about $15,423 to send students home.

blocks.title: Army extends the City of Leavenworth's sewage contract at Fort Leavenworth for eight more months as a rate dispute drags on
blocks.text: The Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command at Fort Sam Houston plans an eight-month bridge, November 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, for wastewater treatment at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. This follows a four-month bridge awarded June 30, 2026. The justification says the government and the city are still negotiating "a significant proposed rate increase" for a ten-year follow-on contract. The city owns the treatment plant that connects directly to the fort.

blocks.title: Marine Corps keeps leased copiers running with Cartridge Technologies after a shutdown cut off funding
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Marine Corps
blocks.text: The Marine Corps bought multifunction copier leasing and support for Marine Corps Installations East and II Marine Expeditionary Force from Cartridge Technologies, LLC. The justification says that because of the "extended Government shutdown at the beginning of fiscal year 2026," many activities could not fund copiers sourced through the Defense Logistics Agency, and many periods of performance ended April 1. A Defense Logistics Agency policy exception let non-agency contracting offices keep the regional provider. It was posted as an Award Notice.

sections.headline: Accenture Federal Services wins $74.8 million to run Social Security's Ticket to Work program manager contract
paragraphs: There were 256 new award notices, with 9 repeats left out; 10 were flagged and 246 are routine, about 200 of them Defense Logistics Agency parts buys. Award notices for solicitations listed earlier are included here because the award is the news.

blocks.title: Accenture Federal Services wins $74.8 million Social Security Ticket to Work program manager recompete
blocks.text: The Social Security Administration awarded Accenture Federal Services LLC the Ticket Program Manager contract on November 2. The contractor manages the Ticket to Work Program: recruiting and monitoring employment networks, helping beneficiaries reach them, running a contact center and website, and paying the networks. The contract is cost-plus-award-fee with a one-year base and four option years.

blocks.title: Southwest Research Institute gets a $19.9 million sole-source NASA contract for the HelioSwarm mission
blocks.text: NASA's Ames Research Center awarded Southwest Research Institute the cost-plus-fixed-fee HelioSwarm Medium-Class Explorers mission contract on October 29. The notice cites its "unique qualifications" and the need for continuity on the mission as the reason for no competition. The redacted justification is to be posted within the required time.

blocks.title: Lockheed Martin gets $10.4 million without competition for PAC-3 missile seeker flight tests
blocks.text: The Army gave Lockheed Martin an October 30 award for flight test support of the PAC-3 Guidance Processor Unit Redesign, Seeker Block V, including system testing, data analysis and problem resolution. The notice cites the only-one-responsible-source authority.

meta: base year plus four option years

sections.headline: Air Force prepares to hire advisers to manage its housing, lodging and utilities privatization programs
paragraphs: There were 52 new presolicitations, with 7 repeats left out. Of 9 flagged, 7 had been listed earlier (including the sole-source bridge for Leidos at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency) and are omitted.

blocks.title: Air Force plans advisory contract to manage privatized housing, lodging and utilities programs
blocks.text: The Air Force's 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron is doing pre-solicitation analysis for non-personal advisory and assistance services for the Privatization Management Programs covering Air Force housing, enhanced use leases, lodging and utilities. An update says no offers will be accepted, and only questions about the requirements are being taken. Eighteen attached files are queued.

sections.headline: Navy says the F-35 Joint Program Office security services request for proposals will come before the end of 2026
paragraphs: There were 48 new special notices, with 5 repeats left out. Of 20 flagged, 18 had been listed earlier and are omitted, including the Joint Task Force Southern Border industry briefing.

blocks.title: Navy says it will issue the F-35 program office security services request for proposals before year-end
blocks.text: The Navy's Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division says it plans to issue the formal request for proposals for F-35 Joint Strike Fighter Joint Program Office Security Services before the end of calendar 2026. It requests no information from industry now. The number changed from N0042126R1004.

blocks.title: Defense Intelligence Agency seeks industry input on the next Solutions for Intelligence Analysis contract
blocks.text: The Defense Intelligence Agency's Virginia Contracting Activity issued a request for information for non-personal services under the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 indefinite-delivery contract. The notice says no request for proposals exists yet and no contract will be awarded from the request.

Late document finding: a file read today on a notice posted earlier says the Transportation Security Administration will limit qualification testing for second-generation Advanced Imaging Technology to the first three applicants per track (70T04026QPL7672AIT001). Routine special notices include NASA, 3, and Naval Research Laboratory, 2.

sections.headline: Air Force at RAF Lakenheath seeks an AI-enabled maintenance decision-support platform
paragraphs: There were 100 new sources sought notices, with 3 repeats left out. Of 20 flagged, 12 had been listed earlier (including two Secret Service requests) and are omitted.

blocks.title: Air Force at RAF Lakenheath seeks AI software to guide vehicle and aircraft maintenance
blocks.text: The Air Force's 48th Contracting Squadron, for the 100th Maintenance Group, seeks commercial vendors for an AI-enabled maintenance decision-support and edge computing platform. It would take in technical orders, maintenance manuals, historical records and live vehicle telematics to walk technicians through troubleshooting. Two files are queued.

blocks.title: Special Operations Command seeks proprietary pediatric training materials for combat medics
meta: Department of Defense, U.S. Special Operations Command
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Special Operations Command is surveying sources for American Academy of Pediatrics PEPP training materials, 210 provider manuals plus 2,000 online access vouchers a year. The notice says PEPP certification is mandatory for Special Operations combat medics.

blocks.title: Army seeks cross-domain security solutions for enterprise and battlefield networks
blocks.text: The Army's Product Manager Communications Security is doing market research on commercial and government cross-domain solutions that meet the National Cross Domain Strategy and Management Office "Raise the Bar" 5.1 or newer guidelines. The systems must work in data centers, vehicles and small expeditionary nodes.

sections.headline: NASA adds $91 million for Boeing's Space Launch System stages contract
paragraphs: There were no new awards of $2 million or more (none from the Defense backlog), one large modification and one cut. The cut, a $14.0 million deduction on an Electric Boat contract signed July 21, and the other routine action are listed in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: The Boeing Company received a $91,000,000 modification (P00179) from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration on October 28. The description reads "Space Launch System Stages Production and Evolution Contract, funding, UCA extension," which points to added funding and an extension of an undefinitized contract action (work authorized before the final price is agreed). The agency classified it as an other administrative action. (award)
Under $2 million: 8 new awards screened, 3 of them from the Defense backlog. None was flagged, so none is listed.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files or spend plans were approved in this window
paragraphs: No new apportionment files or spend plans were flagged or approved during the reporting window from October 29, 2026, to November 3, 2026. Office of Management and Budget activity remained quiet across all tracked accounts.

Defense Department awards are published about 90 days after signing; those show the signing date.

footer.coverage_window: SAM.gov notices and justifications for November 2-3, 2026 (Pacific time); USAspending with a trailing sweep plus the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases; OMB apportionments for October 29 to November 3, 2026.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. The OMB apportionments pass found no new files or spend plans. Document coverage: 2,079 attachments on 430 notices were found; 95 are access-restricted on SAM.gov, 1 could not be downloaded or read, 12 failed during reading, and 1,338 are queued for a later edition (8,277 files are queued across all editions). About 959 links to outside portals, mostly the Defense Logistics Agency's DIBBS site, were not followed. Findings from queued files will appear as late document findings. One justification (Marine Forces Reserve conversational AI) had only the notice blurb available.
